title: Sheafified free internal modules and the product-tensor linearization
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Work in internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with internal relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Write $A[X]$ for the free internal module on a condensed set $X$, with its canonical generalized generators $[x]$, as in [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction]. Let $E_A$ be the underlying-sheaf-preserving internal-to-section-module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], and use the sheaf tensor structures [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For each condensed set $X$, form the presheaf of $A$-modules $F_X(S)=A(S)[X(S)]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], whose restriction maps send $a[x]$ to $a|_T[x|_T]$. There is a canonical isomorphism $E_A(A[X])\cong F_X^\#$, where $(-)^\#$ denotes module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Under this isomorphism a morphism $A[X]\to M$ is uniquely specified by a natural assignment $x\in X(S)\mapsto m_x\in E_A(M)(S)$, with formula $\sum a_x[x]\mapsto\sum a_xm_x$ on the free presheaf. For a map $u:X\to Y$ the induced map sends $[x]$ to $[u(x)]$; equality of maps out of $A[X]$ is detected on all such generalized generators. For every pair of condensed sets $X,Y$ there are inverse natural internal-module maps
$$A[X]\otimes_A A[Y]\ \rightleftarrows\ A[X\times Y],\qquad [x]\otimes[y]\longleftrightarrow[(x,y)].$$
They are the sheafifications, under the internal-to-section tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], of the sectionwise free-module tensor maps, commute with all restrictions and maps of $X,Y$, and agree with the canonical generator maps of the fixed free adjunction. For the terminal condensed set $1$, $A[1]\cong A$ sends $[\ast]$ to $1$. These identifications respect associators, symmetry and unitors. No claim that $A[X](S)$ is sectionwise free after sheafification is made.

proof.text: Put $B_X=F_X^\#$ and let $i_X:X\to|B_X|$ send a generalized section to its sheafified basis vector. Apply [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property] with $B=A$ and $E=X$ on our small site. It supplies, for every section-module sheaf $N$, the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_A(B_X,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(X,|N|)$ and its inverse $\sum a_x[x]\mapsto\sum a_xm_x$. All coefficients are sections of the same ring sheaf $A$; no constancy is required. In particular, this is a statement about maps from a sheafification, not about its sections being free. The construction uses precisely the module-sheafification factorization of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof: the construction of O_2[F]; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules

proof.text: Set $P_X=E_A(A[X])$. The fixed adjunction of [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A[X],M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(X,U_AM)$, with restriction along its specified generator map. The equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] is fully faithful and essentially surjective and leaves the underlying sheaves and maps unchanged. Thus for every section-module sheaf $N$ the same restriction map $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_X,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,|N|)$ is bijective (first for $N=E_A(M)$, then for every $N$ by an isomorphism). Apply the normalized uniqueness clause of [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property] to $P_X$ with the image of the fixed generator map: it gives the unique isomorphism $p_X:P_X\cong B_X$ identifying the generators. Explicitly, the maps in the two directions correspond to the two generator maps; each composite fixes the generators and hence is the identity by injectivity of the appropriate restriction bijection. This also verifies normalization against the fixed adjunction rather than a newly chosen free functor.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof: the construction of O_2[F]; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules

proof.text: The bijections just established show that a map $A[X]\to M$ is uniquely determined by all assignments $x\in X(S)\mapsto m_x\in E_A(M)(S)$ compatible with restrictions. Its expression on $F_X$ is the finite-sum expression in step 1. For $u:X\to Y$, naturality of the unit in [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction] says that the induced free map carries $[x]$ to $[u(x)]$. Under $p_X,p_Y$ this is exactly the sheafification of that basis map: [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property] makes maps with these generator values equal. It follows that $p_X$ is natural in $X$ and that equality of internal maps out of $A[X]$ is detected on all generalized generators, since the equivalence preserves underlying maps.

proof.text:
For each $S$ define $t_S:F_X(S)\otimes_{A(S)}F_Y(S)\to F_{X\times Y}(S)$ by
$$(\sum_xa_x[x])\otimes(\sum_yb_y[y])\longmapsto\sum_{x,y}a_xb_y[(x,y)].$$
Finite sums and commutativity of $A(S)$ make this a balanced bilinear rule, so it induces a linear map by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. By the free-module definition [def-weil-pbc-free-module], the prescription $[(x,y)]\mapsto[x]\otimes[y]$ extends uniquely to a linear map $s_S$ in the other direction. The composites fix each $[(x,y)]$ and each $[x]\otimes[y]$; expansion of finite sums and generation by pure tensors give $t_Ss_S=1$ and $s_St_S=1$. For a restriction $S'\to S$, both orders send $(a[x])\otimes(b[y])$ to $(ab)|_{S'}[(x|_{S'},y|_{S'})]$, since $(ab)|_{S'}=a|_{S'}b|_{S'}$. The inverse maps commute with restrictions by the identical basis calculation. For $u:X\to X'$ and $v:Y\to Y'$, the two orders send $[x]\otimes[y]$ to $[(u(x),v(y))]$. Hence $t,s$ are inverse presheaf maps, natural in both variables, including restrictions with a noninjective map on the basis sets.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, objectwise presheaf tensor definition; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] with ring presheaf $A$ and module presheaves $F_X,F_Y$. Because $A$ is already a sheaf, it gives the canonical isomorphism $B_X\otimes_AB_Y\cong(F_X\otimes_{p,A}F_Y)^\#$. Compose this with the sheafification of $t$ from step 4 to obtain $B_X\otimes_AB_Y\cong B_{X\times Y}$; its inverse is the sheafification of $s$ through the inverse comparison. Now use $p_X,p_Y,p_{X\times Y}$ and [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] to obtain
$$E_A(A[X]\otimes_AA[Y])\cong P_X\otimes_AP_Y\cong B_X\otimes_AB_Y\cong B_{X\times Y}\cong E_A(A[X\times Y]).$$
Full faithfulness of $E_A$ lifts this isomorphism and its inverse to the required internal maps. The internal-to-section comparison sends local pure tensors to the same pure tensors. The module-sheafification maps are induced by their presheaf maps, so the displayed maps send $[x]\otimes[y]$ to $[(x,y)]$ and back. Every factor is natural, by steps 3-4 and the cited comparison statements.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, objectwise presheaf tensor definition; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text: For the terminal sheaf $1$, the presheaf $F_1$ is isomorphic to $A$ by $a[\ast]\mapsto a$, with inverse $a\mapsto a[\ast]$ on every object. These formulas commute with restrictions and are inverse by the unique basis expansion [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Since $A$ is a sheaf, module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] leaves it canonically isomorphic to itself. Combining this with $p_1$ and the regular-module comparison $E_A(A)\cong A$ of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] yields $A[1]\cong A$ with $[\ast]\mapsto1$. This includes the zero ring: both sides are its zero module.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, objectwise presheaf tensor definition; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text: Check coherence on generators, retaining the canonical associators, symmetry and unitors of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure, def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. The internal-to-section comparison respects these by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. For associativity both composites, after the product associator, send $([x]\otimes[y])\otimes[z]$ to $[(x,(y,z))]$. For symmetry both send $[x]\otimes[y]$ to $[(y,x)]$. The left unit diagram sends $[\ast]\otimes[x]$ to $[x]$ by $1[x]=[x]$, and the right unit diagram sends $[x]\otimes[\ast]$ to $[x]$ by $[x]1=[x]$. These checks detect equality: iterating step 5 identifies every parenthesized tensor of free modules with the free module on the corresponding product sheaf, so the displayed tensors are exactly the generalized generators tested in step 3. At the section-module level the checks mean precomposing with the canonical presheaf-tensor-to-sheaf maps; [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] and the uniqueness of module-sheafification factorization [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] identify these with the stated tensor maps. No surjectivity on sections is used. This proves all coherence identities for the normalized maps.
